stem: In circle M, $m(\overset{\frown}{CA}) = 60^\circ$ and $m(\overset{\frown}{AD}) = 40^\circ$, and CA and AD are adjacent arcs. Complete: $m(\overset{\frown}{CAD}) = m(\overset{\frown}{CA}) + \ldots\ldots = \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots = \ldots\ldots^\circ$. Drag A, B and C to set the central angle that gives the measure of arc CAD.
solution: CA and AD are adjacent arcs, so m(CAD) = m(CA) + m(AD).
m(CAD) = 100°, and the arc has the same measure as its central angle.

hints.text: The arc measure is the measure of its central angle itself. Check which angle you have set.
Adjacent arcs share one endpoint and add up. Check that you set the arc, not the one across from it.
Add the measures of the two adjacent arcs.
